pass_a_gloss: If anyone among you seems to himself to be wise in this age, let him become a fool (1 Cor 3:18). Attend: he did not only cry, 'Be a fool and senseless,' but 'that you may become wise.' If therefore there is a blameworthy wisdom, according to which 'the sons of this age are wiser than the sons of light in this generation' (Luke 16:8), God is good, who overturns diversities by contraries, that what was said may be fulfilled: 'his end will be a fool.' When will his end be a fool? It is necessary that Christ 'reign until God puts all his enemies under his feet'; and when he has subjected all things to him, 'the last enemy, death, will be destroyed' (1 Cor 15:25–26). When death has been destroyed, then will be the utmost of the partridge, and his end will become a fool. These things about the partridge. The beginning of the second chapter that was read is this: 'A throne of glory exalted from the beginning is the place of our sanctification; our endurance, the endurance of Israel. Lord, all who have forsaken you shall be confounded; departing, they shall be written upon the earth, because they have forsaken the fountain of life, the Lord.' Isaiah the blessed prophet, seeing the Lord and his kingdom, said: 'I saw the Lord of hosts sitting upon a throne high and lifted up' (Isa 6:1). Jeremiah also saw how God reigns; therefore glorifying him he says: 'A throne of glory exalted from the beginning is the place of our sanctification.' Whether you wish to understand these things of Christ, you will not err; or of the Father, you will not think impiously: for the Savior is a throne of glory high and from the beginning. 'Throne of glory,' because his kingdom is high; and 'our sanctification' is Christ; for 'he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all of one.' 'Endurance of Israel': just as the Savior is absolute righteousness, absolute truth, absolute sanctification, so also absolute endurance. And it is not possible to be righteous apart from Christ, nor holy apart from him, nor to endure without having Christ. For he himself is the endurance of Israel. And if you refer it to God, not even so do you go wrong.
